transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-11 16:30 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Khanna (Redwood SE), Marco Silva (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Aurora Head of ML), Luca Romano (CTO), Sean Patel (Platform)

Summary:
Aurora is a hardware-edge startup building sensor analytics. They want a fast PLG path to test Redwood hosted API with free credits, measure time-to-first-token and latency on mid-sized prompts (256-512 tokens). Long-term they may require Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) for compliance and offline batch scoring. Security (KMS, audit logs, SOC2) and cost/latency tradeoffs are key. Next steps: quickstart credits, security pack, and an SE-led benchmark.

Topics: onboarding credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT), hosted vs dedicated vs private, VPC/KMS, quantization, batching, SLA needs, cost per token

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood, with Priya our SE. Quick intros?
[00:18] Maya: Hi, I'm Maya, head of ML at Aurora. We do edge camera analytics, latency sensitive but budget conscious.
[00:27] Luca: Luca here CTO, main concern is if we move away from our in-house runner, how quickly can we get up and verify latency and cost.
[00:35] Priya: Great, thanks. We'll run through options — quick self-serve hosted path first, then dedicated pools and private V P C on-prem options.
[00:46] Sean: Quick thing — we may have to keep PII in-house for certain customers, but for prototype traffic it's ok to use hosted.
[00:55] Jordan: Perfect, that's exactly the typical path: start hosted with credits to get to first token then evaluate dedicated or private for volume or compliance.
[01:10] Maya: What's your typical time-to-first-token? I mean from sign-up to successful inference with our payloads.
[01:18] Priya: For PLG self-serve it's usually under an hour to go from signup to a sample call; TTFT to production-like confidence — depends on your payloads and evals — but first meaningful latency numbers are often available within a day once we give you the benchmark endpoints and test fixtures.
[01:36] Luca: When you say latency numbers, are those p95 numbers or average?
[01:40] Priya: We show p50/p90/p95 in the console. For hosted small models p95 for 256 tokens often in the 120-220 ms range on our infra, larger models and longer sequences push that up. For heavy workloads we recommend dedicated capacity to keep p95 predictable.
[01:58] Maya: 120-220 ms for 256 tokens is great. Our prompts are usually 200-400 tokens with a 512 max. How does batching affect latency vs cost?
[02:12] Priya: Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency. We have batching knobs on Dedicated where you can set latency SLOs and batching window. On hosted, our defaults bias towards lower tail latency for PLG traffic.
[02:28] (brief overlap) Sean: Right, so can we tune batching rules per route?
[02:32] Priya: Yes on Dedicated and Private you can specify per-route policies; hosted has smart routing that optimizes automatically but less customer control.
[02:41] Jordan: Important to call out caching — prefix/KV caching can save a lot of tokens for repetitive prompts, which reduces cost without impacting latency for many scenarios.
[02:53] Maya: We do a lot of repeated context across frames, KV cache sounds promising. Any rough numbers?
[02:59] Priya: Case dependent; we often see 30-60% token reduction with good caching.
[03:06] Luca: For Private, what's the onboarding and ops burden? We have limited infra ops bandwidth.
[03:12] Priya: Private deployments can be VPC or on-prem, we provide a control plane and an on-prem package. Onboarding for Private is heavier—couple weeks to months depending on air-gapped needs. We do full handoffs and runbooks, and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.
[03:30] Maya: SOC 2 and audit logs — required for a pilot with one of our customers.
[03:35] Marco: We can share our SOC2 report and audit-log features; we support SSO/SAML, RBAC and long-term retention in Redwood Console.
[03:44] Sean: What about encryption at rest — we need KMS integration.
[03:47] Priya: KMS integrations supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted also supports customer-managed keys in certain tiers. We'll send specifics.
[03:55] Luca: On cost, curious about unit economics. How do you price hosted vs Dedicated?
[04:00] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based per-token/embedding; Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput and monthly/annual commitments that reduce unit cost. We usually model TCO with expected QPS and token lengths to recommend the right path.
[04:16] Maya: If we start with PLG hosted, do you provide free credits for exploration?
[04:20] Jordan: Yes — we typically provide trial credits for quickstart. For this call we'll offer 10k tokens/credits to validate TTFT and latency; if you need more for a benchmark we can expand.
[04:33] Maya: Awesome. Also, we've built an internal inference runner — how do you handle model compatibility? We might want to bring our own finetuned model later.
[04:42] Priya: We support deploying customer models through Redwood in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we offer a curated model catalog; customers can request onboarding of a model and we can run compatibility checks. Note sometimes quantization or custom kernels are needed; our runtime handles a lot of that but SE-led evals are recommended.
[04:58] Luca: Can Redwood handle model variants or fallbacks if a model becomes overloaded?
[05:03] Priya: Yes, smart routing supports fallbacks to compatible model variants by policy — e.g., fall back to a lower-cost quantized model.
[05:10] Sean: For our sample workloads we need around 150 qps during peak windows and ~20 qps baseline. Does Dedicated support burst capacity?
[05:18] Jordan: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; we can model expected concurrency to size the pool.
[05:26] Maya: For the pilot we'll want to push a 2-week hosted test with our 512-token prompts and see p95 latency at day-of-week peaks. What will Redwood need from us to configure that?
[05:37] Priya: We'll need sample payloads, typical sequence length distribution, QPS targets, and any PII handling constraints. Sean can share a sample payload and a small test harness.
[05:46] Sean: Yep I can collate the payloads and a quick load script.
[05:50] (crosstalk) Maya: Timeline wise we wanted results before end of month, is that doable?
[05:55] Jordan: If you share the payloads this week we can get the quickstart live and the first benchmark within 5 business days.
[06:04] Marco: I'll attach the quickstart link and a checklist after the call, plus the security pack.
[06:08] Luca: Any blockers for us to test on hosted — e.g., IP allowlists, VPC peering?
[06:14] Priya: For hosted you won't get VPC peering unless on a private plan; we do IP allowlist options and secure endpoints. If you need private endpoints we can discuss Dedicated or Private.
[06:25] Maya: Competitive question — some teams consider Anthropic or direct OpenAI, how do you position Redwood?
[06:31] Jordan: Our positioning is production-first inference: predictable latency, cost controls, and unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private. We focus on inference economics and rollout tooling rather than just model access.
[06:46] Luca: That makes sense. We'll need to evaluate vendor maturity and roadmap though.
[06:50] Jordan: Totally. We'll share benchmarks and sample telemetry so you can compare.
[06:56] Maya: Good. One more — do you support structured outputs or tool calling? We rely on structured JSON from the models.
[07:02] Priya: Yes hosted supports structured output and function/tool calling patterns. We'll include examples in the quickstart.
[07:08] Sean: For seed data and privacy, can we opt for logs not to be retained on hosted?
[07:13] Marco: We have retention controls; for hosted trial we can disable retention or limit it. For enterprise we can enforce no retention and additional audit controls in Private.
[07:23] Jordan: Ok, wrapping up — recap and next steps?
[07:27] Maya: Maya: Aurora will share sample payloads and traffic targets.
[07:31] Sean: I'll provide a simple load script and sample frames.
[07:34] Jordan: We'll send quickstart link + 10k credits, security pack with SOC2 and KMS details, and propose a SE-led benchmark slot.
[07:42] Priya: I'll block time for a deeper technical bench next week.
[07:46] Luca: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:49] Jordan: Thanks all — chat in email, expect the links today.
